I have been using my iPhone 5 for a long time now - and even then it seemed a bit too big at first. Now that I'm looking for a new one, all I see is tablets. Xperia Z3 Compact and Galaxy Alpha (I think it's called that) seem to be the best choices, but they're still quite big. To me, being able to comfortably use a phone with one hand is most critical. I carry my laptop around with me quite often, so maybe it rids me of some needs that others may find unfulfilled... But anyway, there's my view. Being able to do all sorts of shit on your phone is cool, but to me it's still a phone. Hell, I'll use my old Sony Ericsson on occasion - because I can dial a number with eyes closed, and whatnot.

I'm a bit wary that this would be preaching to the choir, but seeing how well the larger models sell, I think I'll find some conflicting opinions here. Interested in hearing those.
Do you not mind how huge the phones have become? How important is the "mobile" part of a mobile phone to you?

For me at the moment I'm fine with whatever phone can do the following:

  • Answer calls
  • Send/Receive SMS messages
  • Play music at good quality
  • Connect with FM radio

Anything else is optional to me, at least for now.

Regarding size... I try not to go for something that's too big to hold comfortably. And I don't watch videos on my phone, so I don't care that much about how big the screen is or how good the resolution or display is.

Yeah, I totally agree, phones are too big. To be honest, the iPhone 5 is the perfect phone size IMO, my iPhone 6 is pretty damn unwieldy. I used to LOVE texting with one hand, now that isn't possible for me anymore. I think they should have just stuck to their guns instead of trying to compete with a bigger phone.

And the specs STILL aren't up to snuff. I wish I could get the iPhone 5's body with the NFC, resolution, and camera of the 6 Plus.

I think that typing with one hand on any touchscreen is unwieldy. I prefer to use both hands for speed and accuracy and usually just use my Android Wear watch to reply to messages/emails/texts if my hands are full.

That's unfortunate for you. One-handed typing is more convenient for me(and almost exactly as fast) as either two-handed typing or voice commands.

The convenience was felt when I got a phone that didn't allow it, and I saw how often I wanted to type with one hand and couldn't. Like this message, for example...

I recently picked up a Note 4 and found that it had a great "one-handed mode" option. I think that is a great way to solve this problem. You get the best of both worlds. Let me know what you think about that and if you'd be willing to use a larger phone if it had something like that.
You're totally right, there's a jailbreak tweak called shrinkability that emulates one-handed mode on the Note series. My complaints will be gone the moment it releases.
It's funny how the gigantic Motorola DynatTAC brick phone is ridiculed. Yet look at the direction we're going in. Do people even use their cellulars for talking anymore?
I personally stick to cheaper more "mobile" phones, as I like being able to grab my phone out of my pocket at ease.

My first non-Blackberry smartphone was the Droid X. At 4.3" it was the biggest phone on the market at the time; big enough that it had what I considered a usable touch-screen (the only phone at the time that did). And yet, it didn't feel big to me. I'm not huge but I'm...well, a guy, and I'm not 10 years old so I remember how big landline phones can be. Now I have a Note 3 and it obviously makes its size known if I'm not wearing carpenter jeans, but I don't feel like I'm holding an iPad up to my face when I'm making a phone call either. (Yes, I use it for actual phone calls!)

I'm a huge fan of large phones but I would definitely like to see phones produced in both larger and smaller form factors. I do a lot of media consumption and non-traditional work on my phone and would love to see a high-end phone with a large (6+ inch) screen. My smartphone does a lot of stuff and carries a lot of important info or, at the least, allows access to important info. The only reason I have a laptop these days is because sometimes my phone isn't big enough or I need a full desktop OS.

I don't want to say that large phones are perfect but they cover most of my day-to-day needs until I get home to my desktop PC.
